data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 1 as n \u2192 \u221e (probability of consensus approaches 1, i.e. is 1 - o(1)): no locally stable mixed obstruction survives on a random 3-regular graph whp. Candidate obstructions are configurations where every vertex agrees with the majority of its three neighbors while the coloring stays mixed; but on a random 3-regular graph, which whp has large girth and is an expander, any such mixed configuration forces the disagreeing-edge structure to be a matching separating large monochromatic induced subgraphs, and random expanders have edge expansion \u03a9(1), so the boundary between color classes exceeds what a matching can support. Hence every locally stable mixed configuration is a frozen structure whose expected count vanishes exponentially in n, and the consensus probability approaches 1 in the limit of large n.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one can exhibit a family of constant-size locally stable mixed gadgets that appear with expected count growing like a positive constant times n (linear in n) on random 3-regular graphs, the \u21921 verdict is falsified.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the Lyapunov function is not nonincreasing under asynchronous majority flips, the drift argument collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If periodic (period-2) orbits absorb a positive fraction of trajectories, consensus probability is bounded away from 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Asynchronous majority updates monotonically reduce a Lyapunov function (total number of disagreeing edges changes by a nonpositive amount in expectation at unstable vertices). Vertices with two or three disagreeing neighbors flip and locally homogenize; the only trap is a configuration where the minority boundary has saturated into a matching. On a random 3-regular graph with girth growing and expansion bounded below, a monochromatic set with a matching boundary must contain \u03a9(n) vertices with internally tree-like neighborhoods; but expansion forces |\u2202S| \u2265 c|S| for some c > 1/3, contradicting |\u2202S| matching-sized relative to min(|S|, |S^c|) unless S^c is O(1). Small obstruction islands (constant-size stable mixed subgraphs, e.g. a 4-cycle with alternating induced attachments) appear with expected count that is O(1) or decays, so whp none traps the dynamics and consensus is reached.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
